description: qou-cds1 Step 25. (1) build_atom_nf returns a 6-vector in the H_3 normal-form basis for EVERY mass number, tritium included, so the corpus's atom model is H_3-valued throughout and the genuinely level-k operator Step 24 left as the only remaining avenue is NOT INSTANTIATED anywhere — building one is new construction, not a reading. (2) Real beta-minus decays are HYPERBOLIC: n->protium +6.52, tritium->He3 +4.46, C14->N14 +12.95, against the bare nucleon pair's -0.0358. Ellipticity is a property of the near-degenerate n/p pair, not of beta decay. (3) Exhaustive scan of all 105 species pairs: 21 are elliptic with eigenphases spanning 0.2495..2.9686, and the required 0.0565947 is BELOW ALL of them, the smallest by 4.4x. CORRECTS Step 23: its random control (8.9 %) was against random vectors; against the corpus's own species 20 % of pairs are elliptic, so 'structural' should not have been read as 'special'. The mechanism stands and is confirmed — n-p has the smallest |disc| of the 21, i.e. marginal ellipticity, exactly what a 0.43 % alignment excess predicts.

context.axis: qou-cds1: is there a level-k operator, and do real decays help?
context.answer: No and no. The corpus is H_3-valued at every A, so the level-k avenue is uninstantiated; real nuclear beta decays are all hyperbolic; and across every species pair the required phase is smaller than any available eigenphase.
context.corrects: Step 23's significance claim. Its mechanism stands and is confirmed by n-p having the smallest |disc| of the 21 elliptic pairs, but ellipticity is common (20 % of corpus pairs), so 'structural' must not be read as 'special'.
